hostPath.summary: One command entry, one authority action: the static manager entry is what a caller invokes, and the manager's own SNet_AuthorativeAction carries the command to the host's DoTerminalCommandValidation/DoTerminalCommand pair, which forwards it to the addressed terminal's own SyncIncomingTerminalCommand. Nothing in the managed layer sends a command to a peer directly.

chain.role: the entry the action layer calls; the terminal instance is resolved from `terminalID` by the manager's own registry, which is why the action layer hands over the terminal's own SyncID

chain.name: m_sendTerminalCommand
chain.fieldOffsetNote: declared on the manager next to m_changeTerminalState and m_sendTerminalString
chain.role: the authority action the entry routes through; its own validation/apply pair is the pair below

packetFields.role: the whole payload a command carries. There is no player field, which is why the action layer's `actor` input is not passed on (see `refusals.terminal-command-actor` in door-terminal-hooks.json: the same finding, restated here for the action side).

parsingPath.summary: The action layer does not translate a command name into TERM_Command itself: it composes the typed line and asks the terminal's own interpreter, so a line the terminal does not know can never become a command, and the whitelist is the inner gate rather than the only one.

members.role: the terminal's own interpreter, already read by the observation half

members.name: TryGetCommand
members.signature: public bool TryGetCommand(string inputString, out TERM_Command command, out string param1, out string param2)
members.role: the game's own parse of a typed line

linePath.summary: One line is added through an overload of the terminal's own AddLine, and the line kind is the terminal's own TerminalLineType. The action layer maps the catalog's three severities onto three of those kinds and refuses the rest.

members.name: AddLine
members.signature: public void AddLine(TerminalLineType terminalLineType, string line, float time = 0)
members.role: the only printed-line entry this slice calls. Two other overloads exist (`AddLine(uint lineId, bool spacing)` 0x12954F0 / dump 682127 and `AddLine(string line, bool spacing)` 0x12954C0 / dump 682130); the three-argument form is the only one that carries a line kind, which is what the catalog's `severity` parameter needs.

derivation.basis: actionVocabulary.TerminalLineType in door-terminal-hooks.json names exactly these three readings for a printed line and states that the wait kinds belong to the terminal's own progress rendering; the mapping is a reading of that row, not a new claim

thirdArgument.role: the native member's own time argument. What the game does with a non-zero value is not established by this evidence (the dump gives the parameter name `time` and its default, nothing about what it expires), so the action layer passes the member's own zero and refuses a request that asks for a lifetime with `terminal-lifetime-unsupported` instead of writing a duration whose meaning is unknown.

command.note: That the authority action accepts a host caller which is not the terminal's interacting player is inference: the entries carry no player, but whether the action validates the sender against a session is not readable from the managed wrapper. Listed in inGameVerificationPlan.

basis: AddLine has CallerCount 0 in the managed assembly: no managed caller, so every caller is in il2cpp and nothing in the managed layer proves a send

the replicated terminal payloads are pTerminalCommand, pTerminalState and pTerminalString; pTerminalString carries `ID:uint` and `inputString:string` and is the path of a typed input (WantToSendTerminalString / SyncIncomingTerminalString), not of a displayed line
nothing in the terminal's replicated state (pComputerTerminalState) carries a line buffer
line.conclusion: the action layer treats a printed line as a local effect of the machine that wrote it and reports it with `terminal-line-printed-host-local`; it claims no replication
line.unproven: whether a machine that did not call AddLine displays the line because it re-renders the same replicated command stream

actionWhitelist.basis: the members the action layer runs; everything else the interpreter can parse is refused with `terminal-command-not-allowed`
actionWhitelist.note: the refused and excluded sets are the interpreter's own markers and the sitting player's screen commands, neither of which is an action on the level. The catalogue row's own note in rows.tsv suggests excluding commands with side effects (DEACTIVATE_ALARMS); this slice does not: the terminal's own parser and the terminal's own authority action are the gates, and a command that acts on the level is exactly what the row is for. A request that wants the narrower set can be blocked on the website side without the mod refusing a command the game itself accepts.

objectActions.summary: The four `forge.action.map.object_*` rows are not implemented by this slice. What each one is missing is a native entry point or a resource kind that exists today, not a decision of this slice.

rows.missing: no native enable/disable semantics for the only two addressed map-object categories
rows.evidence: The map-object namespace addresses doors (`door/<dimension>/<layer>/<zone>/security`) and terminals (`terminal/.../<placement>`). The terminal exposes no enable/disable member: the nearest members are ActivateWardenObjectiveItem / DeactivateWardenObjectiveItem (dump 682204 / 682207) which act on the warden-objective item, not on the terminal, and the state machine's own TERM_State transitions, which the game drives through WantToChangeTerminalState(uint, TERM_State, PlayerAgent) (dump 683360) — a player-attributed state call, not an enabled flag. The security door exposes no generic enable either; its nearest member is AttemptGlueMaxEnabled(bool) (dump 688240, a glue state) and the interaction entry the door action row already uses. The catalog's `scope: self|children|subtree` further requires a stable hierarchy identity, which no map-object category has (a zone's terminal list order is a placement order, not a parent/child relationship).
same reading; a disable also has to answer what happens to collision and navigation, and neither category's managed surface offers a member that does both.

rows.missing: a resource kind the row can name, and a native spawn entry whose identity the caller can produce
rows.evidence: Player.PlayerAgent's item path does have a host entry: ItemReplicationManager.SpawnItem(Player.pItemData data, ItemReplicationManager.delItemCallback callback, Player.ItemMode mode, Vector3 position, Quaternion rotation, AIGraph.AIG_CourseNode courseNode, Player.PlayerAgent owner) (dump 582931, RVA 0x12A0290) alongside ThrowItem (dump 582928) and SpawnGear (dump 582940), all replicated through the manager's own SNet replication object (m_SNetReplicationManager_Item). But pItemData identifies its item by `itemID_gearCRC:uint` plus `pItemData_Custom{ammo, byteId, byteState}` — a CRC, not a data-block persistent id — so a caller can only spawn an item whose CRC it already knows; the catalog row's `resource` port is `resourceKind: model` with schema `forge.resource.model`, and the first round has no model resource provider at all (`graphResourceKinds` carries `model`, but nothing produces or resolves one). Neither half exists, so the row cannot be carried end to end.

rows.missing: same as object_spawn, plus an object this slice may remove
rows.evidence: ItemReplicationManager.OnItemDeSpawn(ItemReplicator) (dump 582937) has RVA 0x353190 — the same folded empty body (`ret 0`) that door-terminal-hooks.json records for LG_SecurityDoor::AttemptDamage, so it is not a removal entry the managed layer can call and expect an effect. Removing a level's own object has no entry either: a door is the level's entrance gate and a terminal is registered in its zone's own list and in the terminal manager's registry (GetTerminal, WantToChangeTerminalState), so removing one would leave the level's own tables describing an object that is gone. The rows.tsv note for this row reaches the same conclusion ('only remove objects this mod spawned').

reshapedRows.note: For the website batch that owns the catalog: rows.tsv already marks object_transform as site-reshape and suggests restricting the object set to what this mod spawns. The same restriction is what object_enable/object_disable need, because the native side has no generic enabled flag for a level's own objects. Until a Forge-owned spawned-object category exists (which needs the spawn path above), the honest shape of object_enable/object_disable is 'target = a Forge-spawned object', and until then neither row can be carried out.

unproven: whether LG_ComputerTerminalManager.WantToSendTerminalCommand accepts a host caller that is not the terminal's interacting player (the authority action's own sender check is in il2cpp)
whether a printed line reaches another machine without that machine calling AddLine
what the native AddLine's third argument expires when it is non-zero
whether the interpreter's TryGetCommand fills param1/param2 exactly the way a player's typed line would for every command in the whitelist

host runs the output row with one client connected: confirm whether the line appears on the client's terminal screen; the row's reported commit is local either way
run the command row on a client: confirm the row is refused with `authority-or-phase` before any native call
print a line with each of the three severities and confirm the terminal renders Normal, Warning and Fail
